maker: Tommy Flowers and the General Post Office, for Bletchley Park
summary: The machines British codebreakers used to read the German Lorenz cipher in the Second World War. Colossus is regarded as the first programmable, electronic, digital computer: it used vacuum tubes (valves) where earlier machines used relays. It was kept secret for decades, so it had little influence on the computers that followed.

events.note: Design and building start at the Post Office research station.
The first Colossus is delivered to Bletchley Park.
The last machines are taken out of use and dismantled around this time.

cause: Dismantled in secret once it was no longer needed for codebreaking.
